chunks.text:
I spent the last 9 months doing something most people say can't be done alone:
I designed a complete superscalar out-of-order RISC-V processor — with an AI
tensor accelerator — from scratch, and timing-closed it on real FPGA.
	
Meet LOTUS OMNI.
	
What I built (solo):
• 4-wide OoO RV64I core — TAGE branch prediction, checkpointed register
renaming, partitioned reservation stations, 32-entry ROB, 128-entry PRF
• Dual 8×8 systolic tensor arrays (BF16 + INT8) with 2:4 structured sparsity
• 3-level cache hierarchy + stride prefetcher
• 2-D mesh NoC with credit-based congestion control
	
The proof (Xilinx Vivado, post-route):
✅ Timing MET @ 80 MHz — WNS +0.141 ns, 0 failing endpoints
✅ Tensor 8×8 MATMUL verified 64/64 in self-checking simulation
✅ 55k LUT / 38k FF / 17 BRAM / 64 DSP — zero latches
✅ Timing closure from −7.019 ns → +0.141 ns
	
I'm self-taught. No team, no shortcuts — just curiosity, discipline, and
thousands of hours of RTL. Everything is open-source, with full documentation
and raw Vivado reports:
	
🔗 https://github.com/Sanuka-cmd-net/lotus-omni
	
I'm looking for internships and junior RTL / digital-design roles where I can
keep building real silicon. If you're hiring — or know someone who is —
I'd love to talk.
